cards.text: The word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel, a priest living in the land of the Chaldeans (Ezekiel 1:3). God calls him "Son of man" and opens with a question about the wood of the vine. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer next to a key that NEVER figured out which door it opened, so when somebody asks a question, I lean all the way in.

cards.question: God asks Ezekiel how the wood of the vine measures up against something else. Against what?

answers.text: The branches of the forest trees
The reeds of the Nile river
The stalks of the wheat field

cards.text: Then God gets down to it: can you make ANYTHING useful out of vine wood? Not a table, not a door, friend, I mean the tiniest, most bottom-of-the-list job a piece of wood could ever get.

cards.question: God asks if vine wood can even be made into a ___ to hang utensils on.
Vine wood can't be made into anything useful. So what does God say happens to it?

answers.text: It is cast into the fire for fuel
It is carved into a walking staff
It is left to rot in the field

cards.text: The fire devours both ends and chars the middle, and God asks if it can be useful for anything now. Friend, that's my first batch the day the oven timer quit: ends GONE, middle black, and me holding up the tray asking, "Can we call this crispy?"

cards.question: True or false: God says that even when the vine wood was whole, before any fire touched it, it still couldn't be made useful.

cards.text: Then it turns. I was sitting here thinking we'd signed up for a woodworking class, and then comes "Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says:"

cards.question: Like the vine wood He has given to the fire for fuel, God says He will give up a people. Which people?

cards.text: God says He will set His face against them. Not a glance, friend, His FACE, and I think the next line is the hardest one in this whole message.

cards.question: True or false: God says the people of Jerusalem who have escaped the fire are safe for good.
When God sets His face against the people of Jerusalem, what does He tell Ezekiel will be known?

answers.text: That the vine will grow back

cards.text: Last line. God says He will make the land desolate, and unlike that key from my drawer, nobody's left guessing on this one: He says exactly why.

cards.question: God says He will make the land desolate because the people have acted ___.

findings.problem: The key joke doesn't match the core action. The moment is God asking a question. The comparison is a key that never figured out which door it opens, which is about not knowing its own purpose, not about being asked something. The step to 'so I lean all the way in' doesn't follow, and a stranger would say 'huh?'.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The question asks what vine wood could be made into 'to hang utensils on.' Neither wrong answer is believable for that job: a yoke and a spear are not things you hang utensils on. 'peg' stands out as the only answer that fits, so the card tests nothing.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The question opens with 'Vine wood can't be made into anything useful.' That rules out the wrong answer 'It is carved into a walking staff,' because a staff is a useful thing made from the wood.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The statement says 'the people of Jerusalem who have escaped the fire' as if it were fact. Ezekiel 15:7 says 'Though they may have escaped the fire.' The 'though' and 'may have' are dropped.

No card ever says that 'yet another fire will consume them' (Ezekiel 15:7). The true/false answer 'False' only tells the baker the people aren't safe. They never learn about the second fire, which ties the vine picture to Jerusalem.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
